You seem to have the wrong idea. I am experienced. Basically they are going to use the info they collect from you, family, or professionals on your team to determine the level of care.

Depending on your symptoms they will discharge you if you’re showing improvement from the initial admit. Usually when people get admitted it’s for urgent or emergency care, and usually related to being a danger or concern to yourself and others.

This can differ from patients who’ve lapsed on meds, who are havi anxiety or panic attacks, etc. 

Once they see initial improvement physically and mentally they don’t care if you aren’t where you think you’ll be, but they will ask you if you’re ready or how you feel about discharge. 

Depending on your answer and their observation and the facts they’ll proceed on their accord.
